title: P-DAC: Power-Efficient Photonic Accelerators for LLM Inference
problem: Optical analog computing accelerators (e.g., LighteningTransformer) require electrical DAC control to modulate optical intensity modulators; DAC power consumption significantly undermines energy efficiency of photonic systems.
motivation: Photonic accelerators offer exceptional speed and low energy for AI workloads, but practical implementation requires electrical signal conversion that consumes substantial power, negating photonic advantages.
method: P-DAC solution reducing DAC power consumption in optical accelerator control loop; optimizes electrical modulation of Mach-Zehnder modulators and DAC efficiency.
key_novelty: First work targeting DAC power consumption as bottleneck in photonic transformer acceleration.
contributions: P-DAC architecture reducing DAC power in optical accelerator control
Analysis of DAC power consumption in photonic accelerators
Techniques to maintain optical intensity modulation efficiency
Enhanced overall energy efficiency of optical LLM accelerators
limitations: Specific power reduction percentages and performance metrics not quantified in abstract; comparison with electronic GPUs not provided.
primary_theme: DAC power optimization in photonic LLM accelerators
